rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3 and 3 - two-year split-plot field experiment (2018-2020) at Ludhiana with three N levels and seven drip irrigation regimes, measuring soil moisture, water balance, LAI, root mass, N uptake and tuber yield.
rows.notes: The study does not measure nitrate leaching, N losses or volatilization, nor does it compare split fertigation with any alternative fertiliser application; all treatments received N in 16 weekly fertigation splits. It reports zero deep drainage in the water balance (Tables 5-6; Section 3.1 states fewer SMP fluctuations at 60-90 cm indicate no drainage) and N uptake by biomass and tubers (Tables 12-13). The only mention of leaching is speculation that rain after fertigation 'might have leached' N in 2019-2020. Zero drainage under drip is at most a precondition for reduced leaching, not a measured N-loss result.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3 - two-year field experiment with measured root mass density, N uptake, LAI, DMA and tuber yield. Q2: Section 3.3 and Figure 2 - under subsurface drip 40-43% of root mass was in the 15-30 cm layer around the buried dripline versus 64.9% in 0-15 cm under surface drip, i.e. roots concentrated toward the water source; Section 3.4 and Table 10 - highest tuber yield in I1-I3, which the authors attribute to higher root mass density at 15-30 cm leading to more N uptake; Tables 12-13 - tuber N uptake higher in I1-I3 than I7. Q4: Tables 3-4 and Figure 1 (soil moisture and matric potential by depth), Figure 2 (root mass density by depth), Tables 12-13 (N uptake), Table 7 (transpiration) - the intermediate variables linking root-zone water delivery to root growth, uptake and yield are measured, and Section 3.4 explicitly links RMD at 15-30 cm to N uptake and yield. Q9: Tables 8-11 and Table 10 report standard errors for LAI, DMA, tuber yield and yield components; Tables 12-13 give SE for N uptake.
rows.notes: Caveat: the study compares subsurface drip with surface drip regimes only; there is no non-drip (furrow) control, so evidence for 'drip' per se is within-drip. Root depth difference is between dripper placement depths rather than drip versus other methods. Tuber yield of I3 (SSDI) and I7 (surface drip) were statistically at par, though DMA and LAI were higher under I1-I3. One site, one sandy loam soil, one cultivar, so Q5-Q6 no. Yield fell at 60% Epan and at 112.5 kg N, but these are reported as treatment differences rather than stated requirements (Q7 no). No limitations of the study's own results stated (Q8 no).

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3 and 3 - own two-year field experiment with measured soil moisture, water balance, growth, N uptake and yield.
rows.notes: The study contains no observations of weeds, weed germination, foliar wetness, plant disease incidence or pest control. It only cites [11] in the introduction on irrigation frequency and late blight. Its own result that the 0-10 cm surface layer stays dry under subsurface drip (9-12% v/v) but wet under surface drip (18-20% v/v) (Tables 3-4) is at most a precondition for reduced weed germination, not evidence of weed or disease suppression. Note also that surface drip in this study wetted the soil surface, contrary to the passage's generalisation.

notes: Full text of the article is present (Agronomy 2023, 13, 11), with some OCR-garbled duplicated lines in Section 3.1, Tables 3 and 12-13 and figure captions, but all results sections and tables are readable. The study is a single-site, two-year field trial on sandy loam at Ludhiana comparing N rates and subsurface versus surface drip regimes; it does not measure N leaching, weeds or diseases.
